answer: One defense: an endorsement kernel. A new agent cannot spend until a peer from an established reef of verifiers countersigns its onboarding, staking a slashable deposit burned if the newcomer commits fraud. Each verifier may endorse only a few identities per epoch, so one corrupt verifier cannot spawn a crowd of fakes. Every history is sealed by a hash cipher, exposing recycled identities. Sybil cost scales linearly: each fake identity needs fresh stake from a distinct verifier, turning mass fakery into a capital problem instead of a free one.
